deploy-bot: Deploy started: service=redwood-server release=redwood-server@v1.8.3 env=prod started_by=alex commit=abc123

alex: Canary looked fine, pushed to prod at 03:12 UTC. Seeing a spike in 5xxs on /v1/generate (from ~0.1% to ~2.4%). Watching for 5m window. If >1% sustained, will roll back.

maria: Oncall here — I see repeated OOM traces from model-worker shards in the logs, plus increased latencies. No DB migration in release notes.

chris: Confirming — release notes show no schema changes. Automated rollback policy: triggers if 5xx>1% for 3m or latency p95 > 2s for 5m. Looks eligible.

alex: Given OOMs, prefer manual rollback to be safe and pin traffic back to v1.8.2. I'll hold on notifying customers until we confirm. Change window is still open (02:00-05:00 UTC).

priyanka: I'm starting manual rollback now. Running:```bash
deployctl rollback --service redwood-server --to v1.8.2 --reason "spike-5xx-oom"
``` Will watch health checks and draining.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by priyanka. Status: in_progress. Target: v1.8.2. Instances draining: 4 -> 0, new pods coming up.

sylvia: Also pinning route at edge: applied `route.prod.redwood-server -> redwood-server:v1.8.2` to prevent any routing flaps. No additional config changes.

maria: Validating logs and metrics now. OOMs look like they were from the new quantization path. Good catch.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Status: success. Traffic fully on v1.8.2. Health checks green. Error rate back to baseline (~0.15%).

alex: Thanks all. Will update #release-notes with a short blurb and mark this release as rolled back. No customer-facing incident needed for now, but we'll monitor for 30m and escalate if anything recurs.

chris: Follow-up action: create a patch that reverts the quantization change and add an integration test for model-worker memory under load. Also adjust automated rollback threshold for model OOM patterns (sre ticket).

priyanka: Filing the rollback runbook notes and tagging the deploy job: `rollback/redwood-server/1718501234`.

maria: Postmortem will include decision criteria (auto vs manual), comms checklist (who to notify when), and a change-window note.

alex: Optional: consider adding an immediate pinning step in the deploy pipeline for canary-to-prod flow if model memory changes detected.

chris: Agreed. Good rollback execution — closing thread. :white_check_mark:
